headline: Eurozone Business Growth Slows
what: The eurozone flash business index declined to 51.9 in October.
context: A reading above 50 still indicates growth, but activity cooled from September.
why_it_matters: Europe is a major customer for U.S. exporters, so slower demand can reach multinational sales.

headline: British Business Activity Accelerates
what: The United Kingdom’s flash business index rose to 53.1 in October.
context: Services and manufacturing output both strengthened from September.
why_it_matters: Stronger British demand can support U.S. exporters while influencing the pound and global rate expectations.

headline: Asian Markets Move in Different Directions
what: Japan’s Nikkei slipped while China’s Shanghai index advanced.
context: The mixed moves followed Thursday’s technology-led global selloff.
why_it_matters: Asian indexes offer an early read on chip demand, trade, and investor risk before U.S. markets open.
